subject: Status page advisory: intermittent streaming chunk reassembly failures impacting US‑EAST sessions
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@medihealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Status page advisory: intermittent streaming chunk reassembly failures impacting US‑EAST sessions

Hi Julia,

We wanted to alert you that our status page has been updated to reflect an ongoing issue affecting a subset of streaming generation sessions routed through our US‑EAST region. You may see: 

- intermittent stalls or partial chunks in streaming responses
- elevated p95 end‑to‑end latency for sessions using gen-llama-v2 (cpu/gpu variants) in us‑east
- a small number of 502/connection resets for affected requests

Root cause (preliminary): a cache reassembly race between the prefix KV cache and the streaming chunk aggregator under certain rapid‑fanout patterns. Our runtime team has identified a deterministic trigger and rolled a targeted mitigation to reduce the failure surface while we prepare a full fix.

What this means for MediHealth: most requests will continue to succeed, but you may see occasional truncated chunks or longer tails for high‑concurrency conversational workloads. We are prioritizing sessions pinned to the gen-llama-v2 family and will be routing new traffic away from impacted pools where possible.

Immediate actions we took:
- Enabled a conservative fanout cap and temporary routing policy for gen-llama-v2 across us‑east
- Disabled the aggressive prefix prefetch optimization in impacted pools
- Notified on the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/us-east-streaming-2026-05-11

Next steps and ETA:
- Hotfix rollout (mitigation) completed: 09:40 PDT (in progress at time of this message)
- Full patch that removes the race condition: target 24‑48 hours, with a postmortem to follow

If you have any active runs or demos today that are sensitive to partial streams, recommend either:
- Temporarily pinning to gen-llama-v1 variants (less affected) OR
- Switching routed_region to us‑west for critical sessions until we confirm full remediation

We attached a short runbook with detection and recommended mitigations for your SRE/engineering teams.

We’ll keep updates on the status page and follow up in this thread. Sorry for the disruption — we know streaming UX matters for your workflows.

— Ethan
Ethan Park
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ethan.park@redwood.ai

Thanks Ethan — appreciate the heads up. Two clarifying Qs:

1) Do you have any rough estimate of the percentage of our requests that might see this? We run long conversational sessions for triage workflows and want to size impact.

2) If we pin to gen-llama-v1 in the short term, will we need schema or prompt changes to maintain parity with the model outputs?

Julia Park
Director, Platform Engineering — MediHealth
julia.park@medihealth.com
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@medihealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:41:50 -0700
Subject: Re: Status page advisory: intermittent streaming chunk reassembly failures impacting US‑EAST sessions

Hi Julia — quick answers:

1) Current telemetry (rolling 30 minutes) shows ~0.8–1.6% of requests from customers routed through the most affected pools. For clients with many concurrent sessions and aggressive fanout, that number can jump higher locally. I can share an anonymized sample if that helps.

2) Pinning to gen-llama-v1 should be a low‑risk short‑term move. Output differences are modest for structured prompts we’ve validated with you; recommend:
   - Keep the same prompts and compare a small sample (10–20 requests) before switching at scale
   - If you use output‑format checks, allow the same response validation (no schema changes expected)

Internal note: Marissa/Ben — FYI the mitigation is live but we still see a few tail events. Can you confirm the scheduled rollback window and whether we should enable region routing to us‑west for customers who ask?

— Ethan
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Status page advisory: intermittent streaming chunk reassembly failures impacting US‑EAST sessions

On it — we finished the hot mitigation rollout at 09:40 and are observing a reduction in 502s and chunk truncation reports. Ops will keep the conservative fanout cap for another 6 hours to validate.

Rollback/rollback window: none planned; full patch expected in ~36 hours, will patch in stages to avoid cold starts. If customers request, we can open a routed_region toggle for MediHealth to shift traffic to us‑west; Ben, can you coordinate the routing rule and confirm any cost implications?

I also uploaded the short runbook to the incident folder and attached the opsRunbook PDF referenced in the customer message.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
